chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Does the one in Ihram slaughter his camel or slaughter his sheep?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.' I said to him, 'Does he cut grass for his riding animal and his camel?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, and he cuts whatever he wishes from the trees until he enters the Haram. So when he enters the Haram, then no.'

key_terms.الْحَرَمَ: The sacred boundary (of Mecca or Medina)
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The pilgrim in the state of Ihram
key_terms.فَلَا: Then no / it is not permitted
key_terms.يَذْبَحُ: To slaughter (general term, often used for smaller livestock)
key_terms.يَنْحَرُ: To slaughter (specifically by cutting the throat, often used for camels)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for a pilgrim in Ihram regarding slaughtering their animal and cutting trees inside and outside the Haram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the spatial distinction in Ihram regulations, affirming that slaughtering one's own livestock and cutting vegetation for sustenance are permissible acts outside the sacred precincts of Mecca. It highlights the juristic principle that the prohibition of cutting trees (qaṭʿ al-shajar) specifically applies within the Haram boundary, a nuance critical for understanding the practical application of pilgrimage rites in Shia fiqh. The narration underscores the flexibility granted to pilgrims regarding their animals' needs while maintaining the sanctity of the holy site.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Musa Bin Sa’dan, from Abdullah Bin Al Qasim, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘Can the one in Ihraam sacrifice his camel, or slaughter his sheep’. Heasws said: ‘Yes’. I said to himasws, ‘Can he cut the grass for his riding animal and his camel?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes, and he can cut whatever he so desires to from the trees, until he enters the Harram. So when he enters the Harram, so no’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Musa ibn Sa‘dan from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Qasim from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who is in the state of Ihram: if he can slaughter his camel or sheep.
